name: Darwin Initiative Main

funder.name: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra)

summary: UK government grants of £200,000 to £1 million for two- to five-year projects that conserve or restore biodiversity while reducing poverty in eligible countries, with a two-stage application.

geography.label: Darwin Initiative Round 32 eligible countries (within listed biodiversity hotspots)

reporting: Annual and half-year progress reports, reviewed each year, against the project's objectives (outputs, ethics, environmental impact), plus a final report at the end of the award.

eligibility.rule: Work within both an eligible country and an eligible hotspot or eligible marine/freshwater environment
Promote economic development and welfare of eligible countries as a primary objective
Be neither a foreign government nor its agency, except a government-funded university outside business-as-usual work
Be neither a Russian organisation nor involved in any way with one
Keep annual funds requested at or below 25% of average annual turnover or income for the previous 3 years
Be led by or partner with local or national organisations in project countries, with early in-country engagement
Lead no more than one application per scheme in Round 32
Submit no multiple applications for the same or similar project in the same year to the listed UK funds

status.quote: Applications to Round 32 of Darwin Initiative Main are now closed.

opens.quote: The latest application round opened on Friday 22nd May 2026.

deadline.quote: Stage 1 deadline for applications: Monday 20th July 2026.

administered_by.quote: NIRAS Darwin Initiative Administrator; first point of contact for projects and applicants.

geography.quote: In Round 32, parts of 36 countries are eligible.

access.quote: All applications should be submitted via the Flexi-Grant application portal.

window.quote: Applications to Darwin Initiative Main are a two-stage process.

amount.quote: Darwin Initiative Main invites applications for projects between £200,000 and £1,000,000 that deliver strong results for biodiversity conservation and poverty reduction.

reporting.quote: Projects must provide Annual and Half Year progress reports that are reviewed each year.

effort.quote: Stage 1 deadline for applications: Monday 20th July 2026.
Stage 2 deadline for applications (by invite only): Monday 30th November 2026.

eligibility.quote: Projects must work within both an eligible country and an eligible hotspot (or marine/freshwater environment).
projects must promote the economic development and welfare of eligible countries (see Annex A) as a primary objective.

Foreign governments and their agencies cannot be Lead Organisations, except for universities that receive government funding (providing the application they are submitting isn't for "business as usual" work that should be covered by the government funding, as per the usual requirements).
Russian organisations are ineligible to be a Lead Organisation or Partner or involved in any way with any Biodiversity Challenge Fund grant.
The maximum annual value of funds requested should not exceed 25% of the Lead Organisation's average annual turnover/income for the previous 3 years.
All projects are required to be led by or partner with local/national organisations of the country/ies in which it is based, with the meaningful and early engagement of incountry stakeholders.
Under Round 32, organisations can only lead one application per scheme.

However, applicants cannot make multiple funding applications for the same or similar project in the same year to Darwin Initiative, IWT Challenge Fund, Global Centre on Biodiversity for Climate (GCBC) and/or Ocean Community Empowerment and Nature (OCEAN) Grants Programme.

after_award.quote: Projects must provide Annual and Half Year progress reports that are reviewed each year. These reports must provide robust reporting against intended objectives and include information on outputs, ethics and environmental impact. All projects are required to submit a Final Report at the end of the award.
Projects over £100k but under £1,000,000 need an end of project audit.
all staff from lead organisation and project partners trained in safeguarding and PSEAH before the commencement of any project activities;

documents.quote: Theory of Change Required, on template provided
